questions.text: Why is non-financial information important for financial statement analysis?

options.a: Every non-financial metric is a cash-flow measure
options.b: Non-financial information replaces all recognized liabilities
options.c: Financial statements disclose every commercially important business capability
options.d: Financial statements omit many aspects of operations, risks, innovation, and governance

questions.text: Which is a source of non-financial information identified in the lecture?

options.a: Only the income tax return
options.b: Only the closing share price
options.c: Management reports, sustainability disclosures, audit reports, patents, and insider transactions
options.d: Only the sum of gross profit and dividends

questions.text: What do the initials ESG stand for?

options.a: Earnings, solvency, and goodwill
options.b: Expenses, shares, and guarantees
options.c: Environmental, social, and governance
options.d: Equity, sales, and growth

questions.text: Which is primarily an environmental metric?

options.a: Greenhouse-gas emissions measured in CO2-equivalent tonnes
options.b: Number of independent directors
options.c: Percentage of variable executive pay linked to ESG targets
options.d: Employee turnover rate

questions.text: Which is primarily a social metric?

options.a: Workforce turnover and occupational safety
options.b: Audit fee intensity
options.c: Direct CO2 emissions from factories
options.d: Number of independent directors

questions.text: Which is primarily a governance metric?

options.a: Workplace accident frequency
options.b: Purchased electricity consumption
options.c: Board composition and anti-corruption controls
options.d: Water withdrawal volume

questions.text: Why are many ESG metrics difficult to compare with accounting figures?

options.a: Every ESG metric is reported using double-entry bookkeeping
options.b: They are non-monetary, often estimated, and may use different reporting boundaries
options.c: ESG reports never include estimates
options.d: They are always measured in euros

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)?

options.a: Eliminating external assurance on financial reports
options.b: Mandating all companies to issue preferred shares
options.c: Requiring in-scope companies to disclose sustainability information under prescribed reporting standards
options.d: Replacing the income statement with carbon data

questions.text: Which reporting framework uses the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)?

options.a: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)
options.b: IFRS 3 acquisition accounting
options.c: IAS 7 cash flow classification
options.d: IFRS 15 revenue recognition

questions.text: What focus is associated with IFRS S1 and S2 sustainability disclosures?

options.a: Only IFRS inventory cost-flow assumptions
options.b: Only employee wage calculations
options.c: Only voluntary charity expenditure
options.d: Sustainability-related risks and opportunities relevant to financial materiality

questions.text: Which orientation is especially associated with GRI standards?

options.a: An impact-focused view of how organizations affect people and the environment
options.b: Bond valuation using yield to maturity
options.c: Exclusive measurement of earnings per share
options.d: Cash conversion cycle analysis

questions.text: What is financial materiality in sustainability reporting?

options.a: The difference between gross revenue and net income
options.b: How a firm's actions affect society regardless of financial consequences
options.c: How sustainability matters affect enterprise cash flows, financing, and cost of capital
options.d: The amount of cash spent on preferred dividends

questions.text: What is impact materiality?

options.a: The value of goodwill impaired during a year
options.b: Only how environmental regulation affects the firm's share price
options.c: The fraction of revenue held in cash
options.d: How a firm's activities affect people and the environment

questions.text: What does double materiality mean under ESRS?

options.a: Every disclosed ESG item must directly affect the next quarter's earnings
options.b: A sustainability topic can be material from a financial or an impact perspective
options.c: Only carbon emissions can be material
options.d: Only topics material from both perspectives are ever reportable

questions.text: Why is an ESG materiality assessment important?

options.a: It ensures that environmental risks cannot affect the firm
options.b: It determines which sustainability topics are sufficiently important to report
options.c: It replaces the firm's internal accounting controls
options.d: It determines the market price of the company's bonds

questions.text: What level of audit assurance is described for sustainability statements in the lecture?

options.a: No assurance is possible under any standard
options.b: Limited assurance, generally lower than the reasonable assurance used for audited financial statements
options.c: Guaranteed assurance that every forecast will occur
options.d: Automatic assurance equivalent to a court judgment

questions.text: According to the 2026 course slide, how did the Omnibus I changes affect CSRD coverage?

options.a: They prohibited publication of sustainability data
options.b: They substantially narrowed the number of companies in scope
options.c: They made GRI reporting compulsory for every private individual
options.d: They eliminated the balance sheet

questions.text: In the 2026 EU framework table shown in the lecture, what do Taxonomy-aligned turnover and capital expenditure indicate?

options.a: The number of patents granted
options.b: The share of revenue or investment associated with environmentally sustainable activities
options.c: The value of all employee pensions
options.d: The amount of dividends paid to creditors

questions.text: What are Scope 1 greenhouse-gas emissions?

options.a: Emissions from purchased electricity only
options.b: Only emissions produced by governments
options.c: All emissions from suppliers and customers
options.d: Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company

questions.text: What are Scope 2 emissions?

options.a: Only direct exhaust from company-owned cars
options.b: All emissions from end users of sold products
options.c: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, heat, or steam
options.d: All emissions from independent competitors

questions.text: What are Scope 3 emissions?

options.a: Only emissions from the company's owned boilers
options.b: Only emissions from purchased electricity
options.c: Only emissions from a central office
options.d: Other indirect emissions across the company's value chain

questions.text: A manufacturer's emissions from customers using its sold products normally fall in which scope?

options.a: Scope 1
options.b: Scope 3
options.c: None of the scopes
options.d: Scope 2

questions.text: What is the main methodological distinction between location-based and market-based Scope 2 accounting?

options.a: Location-based counts only owned vehicles
options.b: Market-based always excludes purchased electricity
options.c: Location-based uses share prices, whereas market-based uses net income
options.d: Location-based uses grid-average factors, whereas market-based considers contractual electricity attributes

questions.text: Why is Scope 3 often the most uncertain component of a greenhouse-gas inventory?

options.a: It uses no assumptions
options.b: It is always directly metered at company-owned plants
options.c: Much of it relies on data and estimates across external suppliers and customers
options.d: It is legally the same as Scope 1

questions.text: What unit is normally used to aggregate different greenhouse gases?

options.a: Tonnes of CO2 equivalents (tCO2e)
options.b: Number of issued bonds
options.c: Days of inventory
options.d: Euros per ordinary share

questions.text: What does carbon intensity per euro of sales measure?

options.a: Operating cash flow divided by emissions
options.b: Net income per patent
options.c: Dividends relative to emissions
options.d: Reported emissions relative to business revenue

questions.text: What does a rising Scope 3 share indicate, holding definitions constant?

options.a: A rise in the independence of the board
options.b: An increase in retained earnings
options.c: A guaranteed reduction in total greenhouse-gas emissions
options.d: A greater proportion of the measured emissions footprint lies in the value chain

questions.text: How is renewable-energy share generally measured in the lecture?

options.a: Independent directors divided by board size
options.b: Renewable energy consumed divided by total energy consumed
options.c: Cash from investing divided by total sales
options.d: Scope 3 emissions divided by total assets

questions.text: What is green capital expenditure share intended to indicate?

options.a: The proportion of capital investment aligned with applicable sustainable-activity criteria
options.b: The dividend yield on green shares
options.c: The proportion of accounting expenses paid in cash
options.d: The total liabilities of a green company

questions.text: What is employee turnover?

options.a: Days absent divided by sales
options.b: Number of employees divided by market capitalization
options.c: Total assets divided by full-time employees
options.d: Employees who leave divided by average employee headcount

questions.text: What does an occupational accident rate normalized by hours worked allow?

options.a: Direct measurement of gross profit margin
options.b: Measurement of every environmental externality
options.c: Comparison of safety incidents adjusted for different exposure levels
options.d: Calculation of basic EPS

questions.text: How is board independence generally expressed?

options.a: Independent directors divided by total board members
options.b: Audit fees divided by net income
options.c: Revenue divided by executive salaries
options.d: Employees divided by directors

questions.text: Why is linking executive variable pay to ESG objectives potentially informative?

options.a: It replaces the need to monitor incentives
options.b: It proves that sustainability targets have been met
options.c: It ensures there can be no conflicts of interest
options.d: It may indicate management incentives tied to sustainability outcomes

questions.text: What is the purpose of an external auditor's opinion?

options.a: To state whether financial statements are presented fairly under the applicable reporting framework
options.b: To guarantee future share returns
options.c: To certify that management will never make an error
options.d: To determine the company's product prices

questions.text: What is an unmodified audit opinion?

options.a: A refusal to form any opinion
options.b: An opinion that all financial forecasts are certain
options.c: An opinion that the statements present fairly in all material respects under the applicable framework
options.d: An opinion that misstatements are material and pervasive

questions.text: What does a qualified audit opinion generally signal?

options.a: An inability to obtain evidence on any aspect of the audit
options.b: A complete absence of any audit problem
options.c: A material but not pervasive issue or limitation affecting specified matters
options.d: Material and pervasive misstatements throughout the statements

questions.text: When is an adverse audit opinion appropriate?

options.a: When all statements are fairly presented
options.b: Whenever there is a single immaterial error
options.c: Whenever the auditor disagrees with the share price
options.d: When identified misstatements are both material and pervasive

questions.text: What does a disclaimer of opinion mean?

options.a: The auditor confirms all balance-sheet figures
options.b: The auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to form an opinion
options.c: The auditor reports only ESG emissions
options.d: The auditor certifies fraud by the firm's competitors

questions.text: What is a key audit matter (KAM)?

options.a: An ordinary shareholder's personal investment preference
options.b: Any issue mentioned in the news
options.c: A matter judged by the auditor to be of greatest significance in the current-period audit
options.d: A guaranteed future accounting loss

questions.text: Why do key audit matters help analysts?

options.a: They independently determine the firm's intrinsic market value
options.b: They identify areas involving substantial judgment, estimation uncertainty, or audit risk
options.c: They eliminate the need to read notes
options.d: They make the audit opinion irrelevant

questions.text: Does disclosure of a KAM automatically modify the audit opinion?

options.a: No; because KAMs are never required for listed firms
options.b: Yes; each KAM is equivalent to an adverse opinion
options.c: Yes; every KAM results in a disclaimer
options.d: No; KAMs describe significant audit matters without necessarily changing the opinion

questions.text: Which is a common topic for a KAM?

options.a: A director's vacation itinerary
options.b: The exact preferred color of its logo
options.c: The firm's office decoration choices
options.d: Goodwill impairment involving forecasts and discount rates

questions.text: Why does an auditor often identify revenue recognition as a KAM?

options.a: All revenue is always received in cash
options.b: Revenue recognition involves no performance obligations
options.c: Timing and measurement of revenue can require significant estimates and judgments
options.d: Revenue cannot be misstated under IFRS

questions.text: What might a newly reported KAM suggest?

options.a: A new or newly significant area of audit attention that warrants further investigation
options.b: Guaranteed decline in revenue
options.c: Definitive proof of fraud
options.d: An automatic restatement of the prior year

questions.text: How is audit fee intensity defined in the lecture?

options.a: Cash flow divided by patents
options.b: Gross profit divided by audit fees
options.c: Number of auditors divided by shareholders
options.d: Audit fees divided by total assets or sales

questions.text: What is a going-concern uncertainty flag intended to capture?

options.a: Whether the auditor reports material uncertainty about the entity's ability to continue operating
options.b: Whether the company has no intangible assets
options.c: Whether inventory turnover is above 3
options.d: Whether the board has an independent chair

questions.text: What general lesson does the Wirecard case illustrate about prior clean audit opinions?

options.a: They ensure that all published cash balances exist
options.b: They do not guarantee that fraud or major misstatements cannot later be discovered
options.c: They make cash confirmation unnecessary
options.d: They remove the need for skepticism in subsequent years

questions.text: What does a patent grant generally provide?

options.a: An obligation for competitors to buy the patent
options.b: An unlimited monopoly over an entire industry
options.c: A time-limited exclusive right in return for disclosure of the invention
options.d: Automatic proof that the invention is commercially valuable

questions.text: Why can patent data complement financial statements?

options.a: Research expenditure is never reported in profit
options.b: All patents must be included at market value
options.c: Patent grants are identical to cash receipts
options.d: Internally generated innovation is often not fully recognized as a balance-sheet asset

questions.text: What is a limitation of patent-count comparisons?

options.a: Patents vary enormously in economic value and firms' patenting strategies differ
options.b: Patents are always published immediately
options.c: All sectors patent at identical rates
options.d: Every patent has the same market value

questions.text: What do patent citations potentially help assess?

options.a: The coupon yield on corporate bonds
options.b: The technical or economic influence of inventions, subject to limitations
options.c: The auditor's reasonable assurance level
options.d: The amount of cash tied up in trade payables

questions.text: What is an important publication timing issue for patent analysis?

options.a: Every filing is published instantly
options.b: Patents can only be published after expiry
options.c: Applications are commonly published about 18 months after initial filing
options.d: Applications remain confidential forever

questions.text: Why can strategic patent filing distort innovation indicators?

options.a: Firms may file defensively or for bargaining rather than only commercial invention value
options.b: Every application results in a profitable product
options.c: Defensive patents are prohibited
options.d: Patent counts fully measure competitive advantage

questions.text: Which sequence accurately represents the broad pharmaceutical development pipeline in the slides?

options.a: Phase II, approval, Phase I, preclinical, Phase III
options.b: Preclinical research, Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, regulatory approval
options.c: Phase III, Phase I, preclinical, approval, Phase II
options.d: Approval, Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, preclinical

questions.text: What is the main objective of Phase I clinical trials?

options.a: Initial assessment of safety, often in a small population
options.b: Large confirmatory tests of commercial demand
options.c: Measurement of final market share
options.d: Regulatory approval of manufacturing plants

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Phase II clinical trials?

options.a: Exploring efficacy and dosing in patients
options.b: Completing shareholder distributions
options.c: Only establishing the company's bond coupon
options.d: Testing customer credit risk

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Phase III trials?

options.a: Establishing the share price of a biotech company
options.b: Large-scale confirmatory evaluation of safety and efficacy
options.c: Patent filing with no patient involvement
options.d: Calculating inventory turnover

questions.text: Why can a failed late-stage trial cause a sharp drop in a biotechnology firm's value?

options.a: Its expected future revenue from a major candidate can collapse
options.b: The failure necessarily increases the number of patents
options.c: The firm automatically receives regulatory approval
options.d: Every failed trial creates immediate tax-free revenue

questions.text: What is pipeline concentration?

options.a: Independent directors divided by all directors
options.b: Sales divided by current assets
options.c: The proportion of projects focused on a leading indication or invention
options.d: Share repurchases divided by earnings

questions.text: What does late-stage pipeline share attempt to capture?

options.a: The ratio of sales to patents
options.b: The portion of employees holding options
options.c: The fraction of drug projects in Phase III or filing stages
options.d: The share of debt maturing within 90 days

questions.text: Why might a promising internally developed drug not appear as a large balance-sheet asset?

options.a: All internally generated development is immediately recognized at expected selling price
options.b: Research and many development costs are expensed before strict capitalization criteria are met
options.c: Drug development never costs money
options.d: All drugs are treated as inventories from discovery

questions.text: How can acquired in-process pharmaceutical R&D differ in accounting from internally developed R&D?

options.a: Every internally developed project is recognized at market price
options.b: Both are automatically classified as trade payables
options.c: Identifiable acquired projects may be recognized at fair value in a business combination
options.d: Acquired projects can never be recognized

questions.text: Why must an intangible asset not yet available for use be tested annually for impairment?

options.a: Its carrying amount needs review even though amortization has not begun
options.b: It has no relation to future economic benefits
options.c: It is always classified as cash
options.d: It cannot lose value before market launch

questions.text: How should a cash runway indicator for a cash-burning biotech be interpreted?

options.a: A larger operating cash outflow automatically extends runway
options.b: Cash reserves relative to the magnitude of ongoing cash burn indicate how long funding might last
options.c: Runway equals return on equity
options.d: Runway measures the patent's remaining legal life

questions.text: Who are persons discharging managerial responsibilities (PDMRs) under EU insider-transaction rules?

options.a: Senior executives and relevant directors, together with applicable closely associated persons for notification
options.b: Every retail investor in the stock market
options.c: Only suppliers with long-term contracts
options.d: Only external auditors

questions.text: What are the relevant disclosures of managers' transactions intended to reveal?

options.a: The daily purchases of all retail customers
options.b: All private political opinions of directors
options.c: Trading by managers and associated persons in instruments of their own issuer
options.d: The future profitability of every portfolio company

questions.text: According to the lecture's description of the EU Market Abuse Regulation, when are notifiable managers' transactions generally reported?

options.a: Within three business days of the transaction
options.b: Ten years after a trade
options.c: Only at the end of the next calendar year
options.d: Only when an annual general meeting occurs

questions.text: What is a closed trading period for relevant corporate insiders under the rules discussed?

options.a: A period when all trade creditors receive payments
options.b: A specified period before interim or annual financial results during which trading is restricted
options.c: A ban on all share ownership for managers
options.d: A period when shares cannot trade on any stock exchange

questions.text: Why may an insider purchase be more informative than an insider sale?

options.a: Buying is often motivated by expected appreciation, whereas sales can reflect liquidity, taxes, or diversification
options.b: Buying insiders can never lose money
options.c: Every sale proves the manager expects bankruptcy
options.d: Insider purchases always precede positive earnings surprises

questions.text: What is a cluster of insider purchases?

options.a: Several suppliers collecting invoices
options.b: Several company insiders acquiring shares around the same time
options.c: One company repeatedly issuing bonds
options.d: A large number of external audit opinions

questions.text: Why might a manager's option exercise be less informative than a voluntary open-market share purchase?

options.a: Option exercises may reflect compensation-plan mechanics rather than a new valuation belief
options.b: Option exercises are always illegal
options.c: An exercise cannot change share ownership
options.d: Voluntary purchases must always be disclosures of unlawful trading

questions.text: How does legal disclosed managerial trading differ from illegal insider dealing?

options.a: Every disclosed trade is automatically unlawful
options.b: Legally disclosed trades comply with restrictions, whereas trading on prohibited inside information is unlawful
options.c: Trading in one's own firm is always legal regardless of inside information
options.d: Illegal dealing applies only to physical securities

questions.text: What is shadow trading in the lecture's context?

options.a: Borrowing in the money market
options.b: Repurchasing treasury shares for a firm's employees
options.c: Trading only one's own company's shares using public disclosures
options.d: Trading securities of an economically linked company using information learned about another company

questions.text: Why can shadow trading create a regulatory concern?

options.a: Insider-dealing rules apply only to balance-sheet assets
options.b: All cross-company trading is prohibited
options.c: Non-public information about one firm may be material for securities of a related firm
options.d: Related firms can never respond to the same economic news

questions.text: A manufacturer reports falling Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, but Scope 3 emissions rise substantially. What is the most defensible conclusion?

options.a: All greenhouse-gas emissions must have fallen
options.b: Operational emissions may have improved while total value-chain impact deteriorated
options.c: The firm has necessarily reached net-zero emissions
options.d: Scope 3 must be ignored because it is outside operations

questions.text: A business faces major physical climate risks, but its own direct emissions are small. Which materiality perspective is especially relevant to the financial risk?

options.a: Historical inventory valuation
options.b: The earnings-per-share denominator
options.c: Inside-out impact materiality exclusively
options.d: Outside-in financial materiality

questions.text: A company's actions cause substantial harm to a local ecosystem without a measurable near-term cash effect. Under double materiality, how should this issue be considered?

options.a: It is automatically classified as OCI
options.b: It can never be reported unless it immediately lowers net income
options.c: It can still be material through the impact perspective
options.d: Only bondholders may assess it

questions.text: A biotech firm has five projects, four targeting a single drug indication. Which risk is most apparent?

options.a: High pipeline concentration in one indication
options.b: A guaranteed diversified earnings stream
options.c: A high board-independence ratio
options.d: A low R&D capitalization ratio by definition

questions.text: An auditor highlights goodwill impairment as a KAM while issuing an unmodified opinion. Which conclusion is correct?

options.a: The auditor has issued an adverse opinion
options.b: Every goodwill impairment estimate is fraudulent
options.c: The goodwill must be written off entirely
options.d: The valuation involved significant audit judgment but the opinion is not necessarily modified

questions.text: Several senior executives voluntarily purchase substantial shares after a price decline. Why might analysts regard this as more informative than a single small sale?

options.a: Executive purchases automatically increase revenue
options.b: Every executive purchase guarantees a positive next-quarter return
options.c: An insider sale is always illegal
options.d: A purchase cluster may reflect shared positive private assessments, though it is not conclusive

questions.text: A company lists 200 patent filings but has low citation counts and no commercialization results. Which analysis is strongest?

options.a: The company necessarily earns higher ROE than peers
options.b: Every patent has a guaranteed equal present value
options.c: Its future earnings are certain because of filing volume
options.d: Patent volume alone is insufficient evidence of economically valuable innovation
